::: {style="max-width: 1100px; margin: 50px auto; text-align: justify;"}

I was a Research Engineer in the Intelligent Machines and Materials Lab, part of Collaborative Robotics and Intelligent Systems (CoRIS) Institute at Oregon State University. I developed hardware for integrating flexible electronics to underwater robots. My work sits at the intersection of mechanical design, robotics, and materials.

Outside of work, I am a virtual pilot and hobbyist photographer.

## Skills

**Mechanical Design & CAD**

CAD Modeling: SolidWorks and Autodesk Fusion 360 for designing soft robotic systems, end effectors, and mechanical metamaterials. I have some experience with Autodesk Inventor.

**Additive Manufacturing**

FDM Printing: Prusa printers for rapid prototyping of gripper fingers and structural components.\
Stereolithography: Printing auxetic materials using the Carbon M1 3D printer for high-resolution parts requiring fine detail.\
Material Jetting: Stratasys J750 for multi-material 3D printing.\
Silicone Casting: Creating molds and elastomer components to fabricate soft robots.

**Simulation & Analysis**

FEA: Ansys Mechanical for structural analysis for soft actuators, including parametric design studies.\
CFD: Ansys Fluent for fundamental fluid flow and heat transfer analysis in packed bed columns and microchannels.\
Material Testing: Instron Universal Testing System for characterizing auxetic metamaterials, and estimating mechanical properties using ASTM's standard testing procedure.

**Programming**

MATLAB: Data processing and visualization\
Python: Building visualization tools for robotics feedback.

**Research Communication**

Experiment Design · Scientific and Technical writing · Presentation
